title: Transport of evaluation comparisons through a monoidal square
statement:
Let $\mathcal C_A,\mathcal C_B,\mathcal D_A,\mathcal D_B$ be symmetric monoidal closed categories: each has a tensor, coherent unit, associativity and symmetry isomorphisms, and natural adjunction bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(T,H(K,M))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(T\otimes K,M)$, whose counits are denoted $\mathrm{ev}$. Let $F:\mathcal C_A\to\mathcal C_B$, $G:\mathcal D_A\to\mathcal D_B$, $U_A:\mathcal C_A\to\mathcal D_A$, $U_B:\mathcal C_B\to\mathcal D_B$ be strong symmetric monoidal functors (their natural tensor and unit comparisons are isomorphisms satisfying the associativity, unit and symmetry axioms), and let $h:U_BF\xrightarrow{\sim}GU_A$ be a monoidal natural isomorphism (its components commute with those tensor and unit comparisons). For any such functor $V$, let $v_V:VH(K,M)\to H(VK,VM)$ be the transpose of $V\mathrm{ev}$ under its tensor comparison. Put $\beta_A=v_{U_A}$ and $\beta_B=v_{U_B}$.

For all $K,M\in\mathcal C_A$, after identifying $U_BFK$ and $GU_AK$, and the corresponding second variables, by $h$, one has
$$v_G\circ G(\beta_A)\circ h_{H_{\mathcal C_A}(K,M)}=\beta_B\circ U_B(v_F).$$
If $\beta_A,\beta_B$ are invertible at the pairs in question, this gives
$$v_G=\beta_B\circ U_B(v_F)\circ h_{H_{\mathcal C_A}(K,M)}^{-1}\circ G(\beta_A^{-1}).$$
The formula carries naturality in both variables, evaluation identities, preservation of tensor–Hom transposes, and preservation of internal-Hom composition for $v_F$ to those for $v_G$ on these pairs. For a third coefficient index $C$, suppose analogous functors, evaluation comparisons and monoidal squares are given for $A\to B\to C$, and that the square isomorphisms respect the specified monoidal composite identifications $F_{A,C}\cong F_{B,C}F_{A,B}$ and $G_{A,C}\cong G_{B,C}G_{A,B}$. If the evaluation comparisons $\beta$ at all required pairs are invertible, the identity and composition equations for $v_F$ imply the corresponding equations for $v_G$, including
$$v_{G_{A,C}}=v_{G_{B,C}}\circ G_{B,C}(v_{G_{A,B}}).$$
Here internal-Hom composition is the transpose of two successive evaluations. Invertibility of $v_F$ is an input if invertibility of $v_G$ is desired; no sheaf-theoretic comparison or essential surjectivity is asserted.

Notation and categorical conventions are those of [def-nagata-category], [def-sfb-monoidal-category].

proof.text:
Fix the tensorator convention $\mu^V_{X,Y}:VX\otimes VY\to V(X\otimes Y)$. Put $H=H_{\mathcal C_A}(K,M)$. For any of the functors $V$ in the question its defining transpose says
$$\mathrm{ev}_{VK,VM}\circ(v_V\otimes1_{VK})=V(\mathrm{ev}_{K,M})\circ\mu^V_{H(K,M),K}.\tag{E}$$
Equality of maps into an internal Hom can therefore be checked after evaluation. The cited uncurry laws use $K\otimes T$, whereas the question uses $T\otimes K$; precompose their evaluations with the specified symmetry $T\otimes K\cong K\otimes T$. Cancellation and precomposition naturality remain the stated uncurry laws. In particular they apply to (E). All later reassociations mean the specified associators, with their naturality and the monoidal-functor associativity axiom, not an assumption that the categories are strict.

source.place: Final paragraph: evaluation, associativity and uniqueness of transpose, and final site-comparison sentence; explicit categorical calculation

proof.text:
Make the suppressed identification by $h$ explicit. Put $P=U_BF$, $Q=GU_A$, and define $r_h:H(PK,PM)\to H(QK,QM)$ by $r_h=H(h_K^{-1},h_M)$. By the natural adjunction defining $H$, it is characterized by
$$\mathrm{ev}_{QK,QM}\circ(r_h\otimes h_K)=h_M\circ\mathrm{ev}_{PK,PM}.\tag{H}$$
Indeed precomposing the right-hand side by $1\otimes h_K^{-1}$ and transposing gives exactly $H(h_K^{-1},h_M)$. Its inverse is $H(h_K,h_M^{-1})$, by functoriality. Thus the first asserted identity, without suppressed endpoints, is
$$v_G\circ G\beta_A\circ h_H=r_h\circ\beta_B\circ U_Bv_F.\tag{S}$$

source.place: Final paragraph: evaluation, associativity and uniqueness of transpose, and final site-comparison sentence; explicit categorical calculation

proof.text:
Evaluate the left side of (S) after tensoring with $h_K$. Twice applying (E), first to $G$ and then to $U_A$, and using naturality of $\mu^G$, gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{ev}_{QK,QM}\circ((v_G\circ G\beta_A\circ h_H)\otimes h_K)
&=G(U_A\mathrm{ev}_{K,M})\circ G(\mu^{U_A}_{H,K})\circ\mu^G_{U_AH,U_AK}\circ(h_H\otimes h_K)\\
&=Q(\mathrm{ev}_{K,M})\circ\mu^Q_{H,K}\circ(h_H\otimes h_K).
\end{aligned}$$
The last equality is the definition $\mu^Q=G(\mu^{U_A})\circ\mu^G$ of the composite tensorator. This uses no invertibility of an internal-Hom comparison.

source.place: Final paragraph: evaluation, associativity and uniqueness of transpose, and final site-comparison sentence; explicit categorical calculation

proof.text:
Using (H), followed by (E) for $U_B$ and for $F$, the evaluation of the right side of (S), on the same tensor product, is
$$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{ev}_{QK,QM}\circ((r_h\circ\beta_B\circ U_Bv_F)\otimes h_K)
&=h_M\circ P(\mathrm{ev}_{K,M})\circ U_B(\mu^F_{H,K})\circ\mu^{U_B}_{FH,FK}\\
&=h_M\circ P(\mathrm{ev}_{K,M})\circ\mu^P_{H,K}\\
&=Q(\mathrm{ev}_{K,M})\circ h_{H\otimes K}\circ\mu^P_{H,K}\\
&=Q(\mathrm{ev}_{K,M})\circ\mu^Q_{H,K}\circ(h_H\otimes h_K).
\end{aligned}$$
The third line is naturality of $h$ at evaluation; the fourth is precisely its monoidality. These agree with step 3. Since $h_K$ is invertible, cancel $1\otimes h_K$ and use the injectivity of inverse transposition to obtain (S). This proves the first formula with the claimed identifications.

source.place: Final paragraph: evaluation, associativity and uniqueness of transpose, and final site-comparison sentence; explicit categorical calculation

proof.text:
If $\beta_A$ and $\beta_B$ are invertible, compose (S) on the right with $h_H^{-1}\circ G(\beta_A^{-1})$. Functoriality gives $G\beta_A\circ G(\beta_A^{-1})=1$, so
$$v_G=r_h\circ\beta_B\circ U_B(v_F)\circ h_H^{-1}\circ G(\beta_A^{-1}).$$
Suppressing the isomorphism $r_h$ is exactly the second displayed formula of the statement. If $v_F$ is invertible, each factor in this expression is invertible: a functor sends an inverse to an inverse. Their reversed composite is an inverse of $v_G$. This does not deduce invertibility of $v_F$ from that of the two $\beta$ maps.

source.place: Final paragraph: evaluation, associativity and uniqueness of transpose, and final site-comparison sentence; explicit categorical calculation

proof.text:
For $a:K'\to K$ and $b:M\to M'$, evaluate the two sides of the naturality equation
$$H(Va,Vb)\circ v_{V;K,M}=v_{V;K',M'}\circ V(H(a,b)).\tag{N}$$
After evaluation and insertion of $1\otimes Va$ where required, both pairings are
$$V\bigl(b\circ\mathrm{ev}_{K,M}\circ(1\otimes a)\bigr)\circ\mu^V_{H(K,M),K'}.$$
This follows by (E), naturality of $\mu^V$, and the defining transpose of $H(a,b)$; injectivity proves (N). Applied to $V=U_A,U_B$, it also proves naturality of $\beta$. Naturality of $h$ and functoriality of $H$ make $r_h$ natural. Thus inserting the formula of step 5 into either side of (N) for $G$ carries the naturality equation for $F$ to that equation on the corresponding image pairs. No fullness or essential surjectivity of $U_A$ or $U_B$ is used.

source.place: Final paragraph: evaluation, associativity and uniqueness of transpose, and final site-comparison sentence; explicit categorical calculation

proof.text:
Let $t:T\to H(K,M)$ and $e=\mathrm{ev}_{K,M}\circ(t\otimes1_K):T\otimes K\to M$. From (E) and tensorator naturality one obtains
$$\mathrm{ev}_{VK,VM}\circ((v_V\circ Vt)\otimes1_{VK})=V(e)\circ\mu^V_{T,K}.\tag{T}$$
Consequently $v_V\circ Vt$ is exactly the transpose of $V(e)\circ\mu^V_{T,K}$. This is preservation of tensor–Hom transposes; setting $t=1$ recovers evaluation compatibility. To see the transport in the square, substitute (S) into (T) for $G$ and precompose its first factor by $h_T$. Naturality gives $h_H\circ P(t)=Q(t)\circ h_T$; monoidality gives $h_{T\otimes K}\circ\mu^P_{T,K}=\mu^Q_{T,K}\circ(h_T\otimes h_K)$. Hence both transported pairings equal $h_M\circ P(e)\circ\mu^P_{T,K}$ by (H). This explicitly carries the evaluation and transpose identities for $F$ through the square.

source.place: Final paragraph: evaluation, associativity and uniqueness of transpose, and final site-comparison sentence; explicit categorical calculation

proof.text:
For three objects $K,L,M$ let $c:H(L,M)\otimes H(K,L)\to H(K,M)$ denote internal-Hom composition. Its defining inverse transpose is the pairing which first evaluates $H(K,L)\otimes K$ and then $H(L,M)\otimes L$. For any $V$, evaluate the proposed compatibility
$$v_{V;K,M}\circ V(c)\circ\mu^V_{H(L,M),H(K,L)}
=c'\circ(v_{V;L,M}\otimes v_{V;K,L}).\tag{C}$$
Here $c'$ is composition for $VK,VL,VM$. By (E), the inverse transpose of the left side is $V$ of those two successive evaluations, preceded by the three-factor tensorator. The right side has inverse transpose
$$\mathrm{ev}_{VL,VM}\circ(v_{V;L,M}\otimes1)\circ(1\otimes\mathrm{ev}_{VK,VL})\circ(1\otimes v_{V;K,L}\otimes1).$$
Twice (E) changes this to the same $V$ of the two evaluations. The monoidal associativity axiom identifies the two three-factor tensorators. Inverse transposition proves (C).

source.place: Final paragraph: evaluation, associativity and uniqueness of transpose, and final site-comparison sentence; explicit categorical calculation

proof.text: The identifications $r_h$ preserve the composition pairings: substitute (H) for the inner evaluation and then for the outer evaluation. The intervening $h_L^{-1}\circ h_L$ cancels, leaving $h_M$ after the two $P$-evaluations and $h_K^{-1}$ on their input. This is the inverse transpose defining $H(h_K^{-1},h_M)$ on the composite. The same two-evaluation calculation, with (C) for $U_A,U_B$, shows that $\beta_A,\beta_B$ respect composition, with their tensorators. Therefore substitute step 5 in both sides of (C) for $G$: the invertible $\beta$ factors and the $r_h$ factors convert that equation into $U_B$ of (C) for $F$. The tensorators used in this substitution match by the monoidality of $h$. This is transport of the specified internal-Hom composition law, rather than an assertion about any unspecified comparison.

source.place: Final paragraph: evaluation, associativity and uniqueness of transpose, and final site-comparison sentence; explicit categorical calculation

proof.text:
For successive functors $V:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ and $W:\mathcal D\to\mathcal E$, evaluate $v_W\circ W(v_V)$. Formula (E) twice and naturality of $\mu^W$ give
$$\mathrm{ev}\circ((v_W\circ Wv_V)\otimes1)=WV(\mathrm{ev})\circ W(\mu^V)\circ\mu^W=WV(\mathrm{ev})\circ\mu^{WV}.$$
The defining inverse transpose of $v_{WV}$ is the last expression, so
$$v_{WV;K,M}=v_{W;VK,VM}\circ W(v_{V;K,M}).\tag{P}$$
For the identity functor with its identity tensorator, (E) reads $\mathrm{ev}\circ(v_{\mathrm{id}}\otimes1)=\mathrm{ev}$, so $v_{\mathrm{id}}=1$. Under a specified monoidal composite isomorphism $V'\cong WV$, steps 2–4 with the other two functors identities identify $v_{V'}$ with this same formula through that isomorphism. Thus (P) applies to the specified composite identifications in the question.

source.place: Final paragraph: evaluation, associativity and uniqueness of transpose, and final site-comparison sentence; explicit categorical calculation

proof.text:
For completeness write the transport of (P) itself. At a pair $(K,M)$ write $\beta_A=\beta_{A;K,M}$ and $\beta_B=\beta_{B;F_{A,B}K,F_{A,B}M}$, with the analogous $\beta_C$. Temporarily express all endpoints through the specified $h$ and composite identifications, so step 5 reads $v_{G_{A,B}}=\beta_B\,U_B(v_{F_{A,B}})\,G_{A,B}(\beta_A^{-1})$. Then substitution gives
$$\begin{aligned}
v_{G_{B,C}}\circ G_{B,C}(v_{G_{A,B}})
&=\beta_C\circ U_C(v_{F_{B,C}})\circ G_{B,C}(\beta_B^{-1}\circ\beta_B)\\
&\qquad\circ G_{B,C}U_B(v_{F_{A,B}})\circ G_{B,C}G_{A,B}(\beta_A^{-1})\\
&=\beta_C\circ U_C\bigl(v_{F_{B,C}}\circ F_{B,C}(v_{F_{A,B}})\bigr)\circ G_{A,C}(\beta_A^{-1})\\
&=v_{G_{A,C}}.
\end{aligned}$$
The second equality cancels the displayed inverse pair. When the $h$ maps are restored, moving them past $v_{F_{A,B}}$ uses precisely
$$G_{B,C}U_B(a)\circ h_{B,C;X}=h_{B,C;Y}\circ U_CF_{B,C}(a),\quad a:X\to Y,$$
with $a=v_{F_{A,B}}$. The remaining $h$ factors combine by the hypothesized coherence $h_{A,C}=G_{B,C}(h_{A,B})\circ h_{B,C}F_{A,B}$, under the specified composite comparisons; the induced $H(h_K^{-1},h_M)$ factors combine by functoriality of $H$. Thus the endpoint identifications used in the calculation are exactly the supplied ones. The last equality uses the assumed $F$ composition equation and step 5 for $A\to C$. For identities the same substitution gives $\beta_A\circ1\circ\beta_A^{-1}=1$, under the supplied identity comparisons. This proves the requested identity and composition transport on all the required pairs.
